newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonds ended slightly higher after a quiet session on Thursday as dealers digested Wednesday's comments on European Monetary Union and awaited Friday's Italian-German summit.
"We'll be watching closely for any comments from Kohl and Prodi, although I really don't expect anything decisive," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
He said the Group of Seven (G-7) meeting scheduled for Saturday in Berlin, could lend some support to the dollar and boost peripheral markets.
If no hard news emerges from the two meetings, the Spanish market will shift its attention to domestic fundamentals, dealers added.
They said a good January CPI, expected to be around 3.0 or 2.9 percent year-on-year, could breathe some optimism into trading. The data are due on February 13.
Spain's yield curve steepened on Thursday, with the spread between two- and 10-year bonds widening to 127 bps from 122.
The long-term differential over Bunds declined, ending at 103 basis points from 106 bps on Wednesday.
